turns.message: What is the difference between FPS and monitor refresh rate?
turns.reply: FPS (Frames Per Second) is how many individual images your computer's hardware can generate every second, while Refresh Rate is how many times your monitor actually updates the image on the screen per second. If your FPS is lower than your refresh rate, you may see stuttering; if it is higher, your monitor can only display the frames up to its maximum limit (e.g., 144 Hz).

explanations.label: Refresh Rate
explanations.explanation: This setting determines the maximum number of times your monitor can update the image per second, which is independent of how many frames your GPU produces.
explanations.catalogDescription: Sets the display refresh rate used in fullscreen modes.
explanations.tradeoffs: Only rates supported by the display are listed; options here are simulated for a 144 Hz display.

explanations.label: Maximum FPS In Game
explanations.path: Video > Advanced Video > Frame Pacing > Maximum FPS In Game
explanations.explanation: This setting caps the number of frames your computer generates, which can be used to stabilize frame pacing or reduce heat.
explanations.catalogDescription: Set an upper limit for the frame rate you can experience while playing the game.
explanations.tradeoffs: A lower cap can reduce heat and power use; a cap below what your PC can render limits smoothness.
